description: Ancient Indian collection of interrelated animal fables in Sanskrit verse and prose, arranged in a frame story to teach niti - wise conduct of life.

tantras.theme: How to break friendships - conspiracies that lead to inseparable friends breaking up

stories.title: The Loss of Friends (Frame)
stories.moral: Beware of wicked counsel that sows discord

stories.title: The Wedge-Pulling Monkey
stories.moral: Do not meddle in affairs that are not your own

stories.title: The Jackal and the War-Drum
stories.moral: Do not be frightened by mere sound

stories.title: Merchant Strong-Tooth
stories.moral: Greed leads to destruction

stories.title: Godly and June
stories.moral: Wicked persons cannot change their nature

stories.title: The Jackal at the Ram-Fight
stories.moral: The fool suffers by interfering in others' quarrels

stories.title: The Weaver's Wife
stories.moral: Deceit begets deceit

stories.title: How the Crow-Hen Killed the Black Snake
stories.moral: Intelligence wins over brute strength

stories.title: The Heron that Liked Crab-Meat
stories.moral: Greed blinds judgment

stories.title: Numskull and the Rabbit
stories.moral: Wit can defeat the mighty

stories.title: The Weaver Who Loved a Princess
stories.moral: Building castles in the air leads to ruin

stories.title: The Ungrateful Man
stories.moral: Never help a wicked person

stories.title: Leap and Creep
stories.moral: United we stand, divided we fall is reversed by cunning

stories.title: The Blue Jackal
stories.moral: False appearance can create temporary power but not last

stories.title: Passion and the Owl
stories.moral: Do not trust flatterers

stories.title: Ugly's Trust Abused
stories.moral: Beauty is deceptive, character matters

stories.title: The Lion and the Carpenter
stories.moral: Foolish friendship is dangerous

stories.title: The Plover Who Fought the Ocean
stories.moral: Even the weak can achieve by perseverance and allies

stories.title: Shell-Neck Slim and Grim
stories.moral: Deceitful speech can cause loss of what you have

stories.title: Forethought, Readywit and Fatalist
stories.moral: Forethought prevents disaster, fatalism invites it

stories.title: The Duel Between Elephant and Sparrow
stories.moral: Never underestimate a small enemy with determined friends

stories.title: The Shrewd Old Gander
stories.moral: A wise counselor detects deceit

stories.title: The Lion and the Ram
stories.moral: Evil company corrupts good nature

stories.title: Smart the Jackal
stories.moral: Cunning without wisdom leads to self-destruction

stories.title: The Monk Who Left His Body Behind
stories.moral: Do not trust blindly

stories.title: The Girl Who Married a Snake
stories.moral: Destiny is powerful

stories.title: Poor Blossom
stories.moral: Kindness returns to you

stories.title: The Unteachable Monkey
stories.moral: You cannot teach a fool

stories.title: Right-Mind and Wrong-Mind
stories.moral: Righteousness ultimately wins

stories.title: A Remedy Worse than the Disease
stories.moral: An improper remedy can be worse than illness

stories.title: The Mice That Ate Iron
stories.moral: Trust should be based on proof

stories.title: The Results of Education
stories.moral: Education shapes nature

stories.title: The Sensible Enemy
stories.moral: A wise enemy is better than a foolish friend

stories.title: The Foolish Friend
stories.moral: A foolish friend is more dangerous than a wise enemy

tantras.theme: Importance of friendship, teamwork and alliance among those with different abilities

stories.title: The Winning of Friends (Frame - Crow, Mouse, Turtle, Deer)
stories.moral: Friendship among different abilities overcomes great threats

stories.title: The Bharunda Birds
stories.moral: Discord over small things destroys all

stories.title: Gold's Gloom (The Mice and Gold)
stories.moral: Wealth can be a burden

stories.title: Mother Shandilee's Bargain
stories.moral: Greed makes you lose everything

stories.title: Self-defeating Forethought
stories.moral: Over-caution can cause self-destruction

stories.title: Mister Duly (The Jackal and the Drum)
stories.moral: Do not judge by outward appearance

stories.title: Soft, the Weaver
stories.moral: One should not covet what belongs to others

stories.title: Hang-Ball and Greedy
stories.moral: Greed leads to entrapment

stories.title: The Mice That Set Elephant Free
stories.moral: Small friends can help in big ways

stories.title: Spot's Captivity
stories.moral: True friends stay in adversity

tantras.theme: War and peace, battle of wits is mightier than battle of swords; choosing good counsel

stories.title: Crows and Owls (Frame - War between crows and owls)
stories.moral: Wit defeats superior brute force

stories.title: How the Birds Picked a King
stories.moral: Do not choose a fool as leader

stories.title: How the Rabbit Fooled the Elephant
stories.moral: Intelligence can tame power

stories.title: The Cat's Judgment (The Partridge and the Hare)
stories.moral: Do not seek justice from your enemy

stories.title: The Brahmin's Goat
stories.moral: Repeated lies become truth in fools' minds

stories.title: The Snake and the Ants
stories.moral: Even small enemies together can defeat a big one

stories.title: The Snake Who Paid Cash
stories.moral: Greed has consequences

stories.title: The Unsocial Swans
stories.moral: Evil company ruins the good

stories.title: The Self-sacrificing Dove
stories.moral: Hospitality even at cost of life is noble

stories.title: The Old Man with the Young Wife
stories.moral: Circumstances change feelings

stories.title: The Brahmin, the Thief and the Ghost
stories.moral: Deceivers deceive each other

stories.title: The Snake in the Prince's Belly
stories.moral: A secret ailment needs wise cure

stories.title: The Gullible Carpenter
stories.moral: Do not trust your wife with a stranger

stories.title: Mouse-Maid Made Mouse (The Mouse Maiden)
stories.moral: Nature cannot be changed - marry your own kind

stories.title: The Bird with Golden Dung
stories.moral: Greed destroys the source of gain

stories.title: The Cave That Talked
stories.moral: Presence of mind saves from danger

stories.title: The Frog That Rode Snakeback
stories.moral: Necessity makes enemies cooperate

stories.title: The Butter-blinded Brahmin
stories.moral: Greed makes you blind

tantras.olivelle_name: On Losing What You Have Gained
tantras.theme: Do not lose what you have gained - cautions against peer pressure and sweet-talking cunning

stories.title: Loss of Gains (Frame - Monkey and Crocodile)
stories.moral: A witty mind saves from deceitful friends

stories.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
stories.moral: Intelligence saves from flattery and betrayal

stories.title: Handsome and Theodore (The Frog and King)
stories.moral: Do not trust an ungrateful person

stories.title: Flop-Ear and Dusty
stories.moral: Do not be swayed by honeyed words

stories.title: The Potter Militant
stories.moral: Do not fight beyond your strength

stories.title: The Jackal Who Killed No Elephants
stories.moral: Boasting without ability leads to exposure

stories.title: The Ungrateful Wife
stories.moral: Ingratitude is the worst vice

stories.title: King Joy and Secretary Splendor
stories.moral: Fate and effort both matter

stories.title: The Ass in the Tiger-Skin
stories.moral: False appearance does not last long

stories.title: The Farmer's Wife
stories.moral: Adultery and deceit lead to ruin

stories.title: The Pert Hen-Sparrow
stories.moral: Over-ambition destroys

stories.title: How Supersmart Ate the Elephant
stories.moral: Wicked counsel destroys the counselor

stories.title: The Dog Who Went Abroad
stories.moral: Home is best - abroad is not always better

tantras.theme: Do not act without consideration - get facts, be patient, don't build castles in air

stories.title: Ill-Considered Action (Frame)
stories.moral: Never act in haste without verifying facts

stories.title: The Loyal Mongoose (The Loyal Mungoose and the Brahmin's wife)
stories.moral: Hasty judgment leads to irreparable regret

stories.title: The Four Treasure-Seekers
stories.moral: Wrong knowledge leads to destruction

stories.title: The Lion-Makers (The Four Learned Fools)
stories.moral: Learning without common sense is dangerous

stories.title: Hundred-Wit, Thousand-Wit and Single-Wit
stories.moral: Common sense beats mere intelligence

stories.title: The Musical Donkey (The Donkey in Tiger Skin / Donkey and the Washerman)
stories.moral: Foolish display reveals true nature

stories.title: Slow, the Weaver
stories.moral: Desire should not exceed ability

stories.title: The Brahmin's Dream (The Brahman Who Built Castles in Air)
stories.moral: Do not build castles in the air

stories.title: The Unforgiving Monkey
stories.moral: Do not quarrel with wicked people

stories.title: The Credulous Fiend (The Demon and the Brahmin)
stories.moral: Do not trust demons / wicked persons

stories.title: The Three-Breasted Princess
stories.moral: Foolish remedies make matters worse

stories.title: The Fiend Who Washed His Feet
stories.moral: Do not trust a reformed villain too quickly

source_note: Compiled from Arthur W. Ryder translation (1925) and traditional lists, cross-referenced with Wikipedia and slife.org Panchatantra overview. Panchatantra is public domain.
